explanation: Searched Mathlib for a statement of the form "a finite (or Finset-indexed) family in a monoid with total divisibility has a member dividing every member": grepped for `exists_forall_dvd`, `exists_mem_forall_dvd`, `forall_dvd`, `dvd_all`, `∃ i, ∀ j, ... ∣` patterns, and for `IsLeast`/`IsMin` versions for divisibility, and read `Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/ValuationRing.lean` (which only provides `PreValuationRing.iff_dvd_total`, `dvd_total`, `PreValuationRing.cond`, and the ideal-order instances) and `Mathlib/Data/Finset/{Order,Max}.lean`. Mathlib's minimal/maximal-element lemmas (`Finset.exists_min_image`, `Set.Finite.exists_min_image`, `Northcott.exists_min_image`) require a `LinearOrder` on the target, which divisibility in a monoid with zero divisors does not have; `Directed.finset_le` gives only an upper bound for a general transitive directed relation, so obtaining this result from it would need swapping the relation, building the corresponding `Std.Total` instance from `PreValuationRing.iff_dvd_total`, and handling `Finite ι → Fintype ι` — more than the one or two routine lines allowed. Hence no duplicate and no clean special case was found.
